statement: The backend SHALL register a vehicle with its vehicle_id, manifest public key and the ecu_id and hardware_id of each ECU, and SHALL reject a duplicate vehicle_id or duplicate ecu_id with CONFLICT.

The backend SHALL return signed instructions for an ECU only when a RUNNING campaign targets the vehicle, the ECU hardware_id equals the release hardware_id and the last reported active version is below the release version.
The gateway SHALL download only the artifact whose artifact_id and SHA-256 digest are named in verified metadata.
The ECU SHALL write a verified artifact only to its inactive slot and then set update_state=STAGED.
The ECU SHALL keep active_slot and confirmed_slot unchanged from the start of staging until an activation is committed.
The vehicle side SHALL record STAGED, INSTALLED, CONFIRMED, REJECTED and ROLLED_BACK outcomes as audit events carrying ecu_id, version and correlation ID.

The backend SHALL create a campaign only with at least one approved release, a non-empty list of registered and hardware-compatible target vehicles, and a policy with expires_in_s between 60 s and 30 days and require_safe_state=true.
The gateway SHALL produce a version manifest listing, for every ECU, ecu_id, hardware_id, active_slot, active_version, confirmed_version and update_state.
After activation the ECU SHALL mark the active slot as confirmed, set update_state=CONFIRMED and raise trusted_min_version only on a positive health confirmation.
When health confirmation fails, the ECU SHALL make the previously confirmed slot active in a single atomic state write.
The gateway SHALL treat an instruction whose signed metadata is identical to the last accepted metadata for that ECU as a no-op returning ALREADY_APPLIED, without downloading again.

The backend SHALL set the assignment state of (campaign, vehicle, ECU) from each valid event report, allowing only OFFERED to STAGED or REJECTED, STAGED to INSTALLED or REJECTED, and INSTALLED to CONFIRMED or ROLLED_BACK.
The backend SHALL apply an event report with an already processed event_id at most once and return the original result, and SHALL reject a different report reusing that event_id with CONFLICT.
The backend SHALL reject a campaign whose declared ECU dependencies contain a cycle, with code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE and a diagnostic naming the ECUs in the cycle.
While a campaign is PAUSED the backend SHALL return no new instructions for it.
The release process SHALL compute the SHA-256 digest and byte length of every uploaded artifact and SHALL copy both unchanged into every release and signed target that references the artifact.
The gateway SHALL reject an artifact whose computed SHA-256 digest or length differs from trusted metadata before any byte reaches an ECU slot; the ECU SHALL repeat the check before staging.
The gateway SHALL act on metadata only when its Ed25519 signature verifies under a key in the trusted key set.
The gateway SHALL reject metadata whose key_id is unknown or revoked.
The gateway and the ECU SHALL each reject metadata whose ecu_id or hardware_id differs from the target ECU's provisioned identity.
The gateway and the ECU SHALL each reject firmware whose version is below the ECU's trusted_min_version.

The gateway SHALL reject metadata that is expired (expires_at <= trusted time), whose metadata_version is below the last accepted for that ECU, or whose vehicle_id or campaign_id differs from the instruction bundle.

The backend SHALL refuse every action in the authorization matrix unless the caller presents a valid credential (else UNAUTHENTICATED) and holds a role allowed for that action (else FORBIDDEN); a vehicle identity SHALL act only on its own vehicle_id.
The backend SHALL write one audit event for every privileged request, including denied and failed requests, containing actor, action, object, outcome, time and correlation ID.
Private signing keys and credentials SHALL NOT be committed to source control; a private key SHALL be stored only outside the source tree and encrypted with a passphrase supplied at run time.
An external error response SHALL contain only a stable category, code, fixed message and correlation ID, and SHALL NOT contain file paths, stack traces, credentials or key material.
The gateway SHALL reject metadata declaring length above max_artifact_bytes (default 16 MiB) before download, and SHALL stop reading once received bytes exceed the declared length.
The gateway SHALL sign the vehicle version manifest with the vehicle key so that modification is detectable by the backend.

The backend audit trail SHALL link each event to the previous event by SHA-256 so that modification, deletion or truncation (checked against an exported head hash) is reported with the first affected sequence number.
The signing service SHALL refuse to sign target metadata for a release that is not APPROVED or whose ecu_id, hardware_id, version, sha256 or length differ from the payload.
The vehicle SHALL replace its trusted key set only with a key set signed by the provisioned root key whose version is higher than the current version and whose expires_at is later than trusted time.
Each signing key SHALL be authorized for exactly one role (root, release or vehicle), and the gateway SHALL accept target metadata only under non-revoked release-role keys.
The backend and the signing service SHALL each refuse a release approval in which the approver identity equals the release creator.
The backend SHALL reject an artifact upload larger than max_artifact_bytes (default 16 MiB) with PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE without storing it.

The backend SHALL accept a vehicle version manifest only when it verifies under the vehicle key registered for that vehicle_id, lists exactly the registered ECUs and has generated_at later than the last accepted manifest.
The ECU SHALL write new firmware only to the inactive slot.
The active known-good image SHALL remain byte-identical during staging, including when staging is interrupted.
Activation SHALL be blocked unless simulated speed is exactly 0 km/h; missing, negative or non-finite speed SHALL be treated as nonzero.
Activation SHALL be postponed when battery voltage is below min_battery_v (default 12.0 V, configurable) or is not a finite number.
The ECU SHALL roll back when health is reported failed, when no confirmation arrives within health_timeout_s (default 60 s), or after max_boot_attempts (default 3) unconfirmed boots.
A power loss at any defined update checkpoint SHALL leave an active slot whose image matches its recorded digest.
Before switching slots the ECU SHALL re-verify the staged image digest and SHALL refuse activation on mismatch.
On restart after interrupted staging the ECU SHALL discard the partial image and return to IDLE.
While update_state is INSTALLED the ECU SHALL verify the active image digest at each boot and SHALL roll back on mismatch.
The ECU SHALL reject activation, boot-commit and health-confirmation commands that do not match its current update_state.
A clean checkout SHALL run all phase tests, the traceability check, the secret scan and evidence generation with the commands documented in phase2/README.md and finish with exit code 0.
Every backend request, vehicle operation and audit event SHALL carry a correlation ID, and an ID supplied by the caller SHALL appear unchanged in the backend and vehicle events it causes.
The team SHALL record median and maximum verification latency for 64 KiB, 1 MiB and 16 MiB artifacts in evidence/latency.csv together with the Python version and machine type.
The gateway SHALL abort a download when no bytes arrive for stall_timeout_s (default 10 s) or total time exceeds total_timeout_s (default 300 s), without staging.
Audit events, logs and evidence files SHALL NOT contain private keys, credentials or bearer tokens, and the audit trail SHALL refuse event fields named like secrets.
The backend SHALL store for a vehicle only vehicle_id, ECU identities, hardware IDs, the manifest public key and reported versions, and SHALL reject registration fields outside this set.
The operator status view SHALL show a distinct label for offered, staged, active awaiting health, active confirmed, failed (rejected) and rolled-back assignments.
Every rejection SHALL return only a stable reason category and the correlation ID, with no other detail.
